results.name: actor_set_target_alert_stage1
results.evidence: Sets unit-record byte at offset 0xb9 for unit index in_ECX (into the DAT_008802c0 'unit' data array) whenever in_ECX != -1, then, only if in_ECX equals the watching actor's current target (actor+0x270), calls the target-status refresh pair FUN_004200d0/FUN_00420290; near-identical siblings exist at +0xba and +0xbb.
results.summary: Marks a per-unit alert/notice flag (byte at unit+0xb9) and, if that unit is the caller actor's current target, refreshes the actor's target combat status.

results.name: actor_set_target_alert_stage2
results.evidence: Byte-for-byte identical logic to FUN_0041fb00 except it writes unit+0xba instead of +0xb9, forming a sequential trio of near-duplicate flag setters (0xb9/0xba/0xbb).
results.summary: Marks a second per-unit alert/notice flag (byte at unit+0xba) and refreshes the actor's target combat status if that unit is the actor's current target.

results.name: actor_set_target_alert_stage3
results.evidence: Largest of the 0xb9/0xba/0xbb trio: for a valid unit (in_EDX) sets unit+0xbb, additionally promotes a state-4 unit record (unit+0x24) to state 5; for the sentinel case in_EDX==0xffffffff it instead clears several actor-local perception fields (0x3c4,0x3bc,0x3bd,0x72,0x74) that are the same fields consumed by FUN_00420290's awareness computation.
results.summary: Marks the third per-unit alert flag and promotes the unit's combat state, or, when no target unit is supplied, clears the actor's own perception/awareness accumulator fields.

results.name: unit_update_active_combat_flag
results.evidence: Computes cVar4 (whether unit is currently 'active' in combat: state 2-3, exposed 0x60!=0, not dead 0x127==0, and either seen by its actor's target, aiming, or state==0xf), stores it to unit+0xa4, and on losing active status clears unit fields 0xaa/0xac/0xae and, for a helper-target actor record, clears actor+0x3a8/0x3ac if this unit was the recorded helper.
results.summary: Recomputes whether a unit counts as actively engaged in combat this tick and clears stale backup/aim-assist bookkeeping when it stops being active.

results.name: actor_rate_potential_target
results.evidence: Given an actor (param_1) and a candidate unit (param_2), reads the candidate's unit record (state 0x24, distance 0x11c, flags 0x60/0x127/0x12e/0x134/0x135) and the actor's own definition fields, combines several bonus categories (cVar2/cVar3/cVar4/cVar6) into a float10 score with a 1/(dist*0.1+1) falloff term; callers (actor_choose_best_target, actor_consider_target_candidate) store the result into unit+0x50 as a 'target rating' used to pick the best target.
results.summary: Computes a floating-point desirability score for a candidate unit as the given actor's next combat target, combining visibility, distance, alertness and prior-target continuity bonuses.

results.name: actor_update_target_combat_status
results.evidence: Looks up the actor's current target unit (actor+0x270), switches on the target's state field (unit+0x24, values 0-5) to derive a status code stored into actor+0x268, and updates an obscured/aim flag at actor+0x27c from the target's object header flag bit 2 (obj+0x106); called immediately after every place that changes actor+0x270.
results.summary: Recomputes the actor's cached combat-status code and aim/visibility flag for its currently selected target unit.

results.name: actor_update_awareness_level
results.evidence: Consumes the pending perception event recorded by FUN_00422070 (actor+0x34a/0x34c), merges it with a per-target-status minimum threshold table (DAT_00655880 indexed by actor+0x268), and advances actor+0x6e (awareness) plus streak counters at +0x7c/+0x80/+0x84/+0x88/+0x8c, setting +0x8c once awareness exceeds 6.
results.summary: Advances the actor's alertness/awareness state machine each tick from the highest-priority perception event and the current target's combat status.

results.name: actor_choose_best_target
results.evidence: Iterates the actor's perceived-unit linked list (actor+0x50 head, unit+8 next), scores each candidate with FUN_0041fd50, tallies per-zone threat/exposure counters into actor+0x1ec..+0x24d, tracks the maximum-scoring unit in local_c, and on reaching the list end assigns it to actor+0x270 before calling actor_update_target_combat_status/actor_update_awareness_level.
results.summary: Re-evaluates all units the actor currently perceives, selects the highest-scoring one as the new combat target, and refreshes the actor's target/awareness state.

results.name: actor_consider_target_candidate
results.evidence: Rates a single unit (unaff_EBX) with FUN_0041fd50, stores the score into unit+0x50, and only replaces the actor's current target (actor+0x270) if the new score exceeds the existing target's cached score, then calls the same target-status/awareness refresh pair as actor_choose_best_target.
results.summary: Evaluates one specific unit against the actor's current target and swaps to it as the new target if it scores higher.

results.name: actor_get_ranged_attack_vector
results.evidence: For a vehicle unit (unit+0x12e set) it reads a seat/hardpoint position (obj+0x23c/0x240/0x244) into the output vector param_1; otherwise, if the unit already has an enemy (unit+0x1c != -1), it defers to FUN_004281f0; when neither applies it instead scans the actor's perceived-ally list to test whether firing along param_1 would cross an ally within 0.5 dot-product tolerance, calling vector3d_normalize_with_length on the ally offset.
results.summary: Produces an aim/attack direction for the actor's controlled unit (vehicle hardpoint or fallback path) and, in the fallback case, reports whether that line of fire is clear of nearby allies.

results.name: actor_evaluate_flank_offset
results.evidence: Pure geometry helper operating on four register-passed float vectors (unaff_EBX/ESI/EDI, in_ECX): computes a 2D perpendicular basis, projects an enemy-relative offset onto it, and tests it against cos(30 deg)=0.8660254 and several squared-distance bands (0.36=0.6^2, 1.21=1.1^2) to classify a candidate flank position, returning 0/1/2 packed with a passthrough high word.
results.summary: Classifies whether a candidate side/flank position relative to a threat and cover direction is usable, returning a small validity code.

results.name: actor_scale_value_by_ally_exposure
results.evidence: Walks the actor's perceived-unit list counting allies (matching actor+4 type) that are either exposed (sVar7) or already alert/aiming (sVar2, via unit+0x308/0x6c/0xa8), then scales *param_1 down as the exposed-ally count grows and clamps it to [0,2x], zeroing it out if too many allies are already exposed.
results.summary: Adjusts a caller-supplied probability/weight downward based on how many nearby allies of the same type are already exposed or engaged, to avoid redundant reactions.

results.name: ai_group_bucket_find_or_add
results.evidence: Linear-searches a fixed stride-0x1c array (in_EAX) of up to param_1 entries for a key (unaff_EBX), returning its index; if absent and the live count (*unaff_EDI, tracked via short pointer) is below param_1, appends a new zero/-1-initialized entry (including a 0x7f7fffff = FLT_MAX sentinel field) and returns its index.
results.summary: Finds or allocates a small fixed-capacity aggregation-bucket slot keyed by an id, used by the nearby-actor scanning helpers to group results per actor type.

results.name: unit_get_combat_priority
results.evidence: For a unit in active combat (state 0x24 in 2..3) with the 'flagged' bit unit+0xa4 set, returns tiered priority values: 4 if fleeing (unit+0x74), 2 or 3 if crouched (unit+0x12f, based on unit+0x122<2), 1 if unit+0x32>1, else 0; used by actor_scan_allies_for_backup_request to rank which allies most need help.
results.summary: Returns a small integer priority ranking how urgently a unit needs backup/assistance based on its current combat sub-state.

results.name: actor_scan_allies_for_backup_request
results.evidence: Iterates the actor's perceived-unit list, and for each ally whose controlling actor (unit+0x1c) has an active backup request (ally_actor+0x3a8 nonzero and +0x3ac valid) and is not throttled (actor+0x3a4 vs ally_actor+0x3b0), resolves the requester's target via FUN_0043ea80, ranks it with unit_get_combat_priority, and keeps the closest per-type/per-priority bucket via ai_group_bucket_find_or_add; finally decrements the actor's own backup-request countdown (actor+0x3a8) and stamps a new timestamp when it expires.
results.summary: Scans nearby allies for outstanding calls for backup, buckets the most urgent candidates by type, and ages down the actor's own backup-request cooldown.

results.name: actor_update_charge_decision
results.evidence: Per-actor tick routine: calls actor_set_combat_alert_flag, exponentially smooths an accuracy value (actor+0x350/0x354) via f2xm1/fscale, notifies squad state changes through FUN_0042d340 with codes 0x16/0x17, scans perceived allies to set flanking flags (actor+0x35c..0x35f) using actor_get_ranged_attack_vector/actor_evaluate_flank_offset, then switches on the unit-definition charge-trigger enum (puVar1[0xbe], cases 1-5 including a call to FUN_00424090 for case 5) to decide whether to start/stop a melee charge (actor+0x358) with a cooldown timer (actor+0x35a), and finally calls actor_scan_allies_for_backup_request.
results.summary: Runs the actor's per-tick melee-charge/flanking decision logic: updates aim accuracy smoothing, squad flanking flags, evaluates the definition-specified charge trigger, and toggles the charging state.

results.name: actor_set_combat_alert_flag
results.evidence: Only acts when unaff_BL differs from actor+0x378; stores the new flag, clears actor+0x379, and if the actor has no cluster (actor+6==0) sets/clears bit 0x80 of the controlled unit's object flags (obj+0x204), otherwise propagates a bit-0x80 flag across every actor sharing the swarm/cluster (walking obj+0x1fc chain via actor+0x24); also sets actor+0x375 when turning the flag on.
results.summary: Toggles the actor's (and, for grouped actors, its whole cluster's) combat-alert object flag when the alert state changes.

results.name: actor_queue_search_position
results.evidence: Only updates when the actor is not already deep in combat (actor+0x6a<3) and the new priority (in_DX) is >= the stored one (actor+0x312); records up to two optional position/velocity vectors (param blocks at +0x318/+0x330) plus scalar fields (+0x324,+0x328,+0x33c,+0x340,+0x344,+0x348); called throughout the file with a constant duration of 0x5a (90 ticks) whenever a new point of interest is noticed.
results.summary: Records a candidate 'investigate/search' position for the actor if its priority is at least as high as any currently queued one.

results.name: actor_queue_look_position
results.evidence: Smaller sibling of actor_queue_search_position: updates actor+0x2ee (priority) only if the new priority (in_DX) is strictly greater, storing a single position/value at +0x2f4/+0x2fc.
results.summary: Records a single higher-priority 'look at' point of interest for the actor, replacing any lower-priority one.

results.name: actor_evaluate_target_visibility
results.evidence: Large per-target-unit routine: for units in active combat (actor awareness fields, unit+1000 threshold) it fetches a datum via datum_get, applies a decaying re-notice cooldown at unit+0x5c/0x58, then computes an alert duration from random_real_range and queues a dialogue event at actor+0x544 with type 4 (list index) through the shared priority-queue fields (+0x546/+0x548/+0x54c..+0x558); afterward it evaluates line-of-sight (dot product against unit+0xe0..0xe8) and, depending on awareness (actor+0x6e), calls actor_queue_look_position to keep or clear the current look target.
results.summary: Evaluates whether a perceived unit is newly noticed/visible, queues a 'sighted' dialogue event with a randomized duration, and updates the actor's look-at target accordingly.

results.name: actor_record_perception_event
results.evidence: Keeps the maximum of a priority value (in_DX) against actor+0x34a, storing the associated data pointer (unaff_ESI) at actor+0x34c, or merging (max) the data value if the priorities tie; these exact fields are read and reset by actor_update_awareness_level.
results.summary: Records the highest-priority pending perception event for the actor, to be consumed by the next awareness-level update.

results.name: actor_notify_target_engaged
results.evidence: When a candidate unit's target (via actor+0x18, resolved through the object-index table) is not dead and the unit is exposed (unit+0x60), it calls FUN_0042d340 with squad-event code 4 or 5 (based on in_DL) and the target's object id, matching the squad/leader-notification codes seen in nearby dialogue-queue functions.
results.summary: Notifies the actor's squad-event system that a target unit has become engaged, choosing between two event codes based on a flag.

results.name: actor_start_search_timer
results.evidence: Stamps actor+0x3a0 with the current tick count (DAT_006f1d6c+0xc), calls FUN_0041f3a0, and queues a search position (actor_queue_search_position) with fixed priority 0x3fc00000 (1.5) and duration 0x5a using the unit's position field (unit+0xec).
results.summary: Marks the start of a search/investigation timer and queues a corresponding search position for the actor.

results.name: actor_clear_search_queue
results.evidence: Trivial wrapper that calls actor_queue_search_position(0xffffffff, 0, 0x5a), the sentinel pattern used elsewhere to reset the queued search position.
results.summary: Clears any currently queued search/investigate position for the actor.

results.name: actor_clear_search_and_reevaluate_look
results.evidence: Calls actor_clear_search_queue, then if the unit referenced by unit+0x1c has a nonzero actor+0x74-style field it calls actor_record_perception_event (FUN_00422070), otherwise leaves it cleared.
results.summary: Clears the queued search position and, if the related unit still warrants attention, re-queues a perception event for the awareness system.

results.name: actor_queue_dialogue_direction_or_point
results.evidence: Accepts either an explicit direction (in_ECX==-NAN sentinel selects an EAX-supplied direction vector, normalized and negated) or a scalar distance, gated by datum_get and awareness thresholds (actor+0x544<0xc), and queues a dialogue-style event with type field set from DAT_00655654 into the shared priority-queue block, matching the pattern of actor_evaluate_target_visibility's queuing code.
results.summary: Queues a directional or point-based combat dialogue/reaction event for the actor, choosing the event subtype from a lookup table.

results.name: actor_queue_dialogue_with_cooldown
results.evidence: Same datum_get/re-notice-cooldown gating as actor_evaluate_target_visibility (unit+0x5c/0x58) but queues event type 5 (actor+0x544=5) using a fixed random duration scaled by DAT_0065563c, passing param_1 straight through as the event's stored value.
results.summary: Queues a combat dialogue/reaction event of a fixed category once its per-target cooldown has elapsed.

results.name: actor_queue_dialogue_position
results.evidence: Only runs when the actor is not idle (actor+0x6a!=1); forwards a 3-component position (in_EAX[0..2]) into the shared priority-queue fields with event type 1 (actor+0x544=1), gated on awareness (actor+1000<7) and a free slot (actor+0x544<2).
results.summary: Queues a position-based combat dialogue/reaction event of category 1 for the actor.

results.name: actor_notify_and_queue_dialogue_direction
results.evidence: Computes a facing/aim direction (param_1 vs actor+0x120), calls actor_queue_look_position or FUN_0042d340(10,...) depending on whether the actor already recorded that grid/count context (actor+0x280/0x28c/0x284), then also queues a category-3 dialogue event with the incoming position in_EAX.
results.summary: Updates the actor's look/notify state toward a computed direction and queues a matching category-3 dialogue event.

results.name: actor_notify_and_queue_dialogue_point
results.evidence: Mirrors actor_notify_and_queue_dialogue_direction (normalizes param_3 relative to actor+0x120, calls actor_queue_look_position, checks a flee condition via FUN_0045bd50 to optionally call actor_record_perception_event/FUN_00422070) but queues category-6 dialogue with the supplied point (param_3) instead of a computed direction.
results.summary: Updates the actor's look/notify state toward a supplied point, optionally flags a flee-related perception event, and queues a category-6 dialogue event.

results.name: actor_notify_unit_state_change
results.evidence: Branches on whether the controlled unit (param_1) is alive: if so, calls actor_clear_search_and_reevaluate_look and, depending on the unit's vehicle/weapon linkage, either evaluates squad reinforcement (FUN_00428420) or a recent-death/flee check (FUN_0045bd50 then FUN_0041f7d0); if the unit is dead it instead directly notifies via FUN_00421af0; afterward queues a category-7 dialogue event through the same datum_get/cooldown pattern as the other queue_dialogue helpers.
results.summary: Reacts to a change in a controlled unit's alive/dead state, running the appropriate follow-up checks and queuing a category-7 dialogue event.

results.name: actor_update_search_target_for_unit
results.evidence: Marks actor+0x8d as processed for unit param_1, and when the unit is not exposed (unit+0x60==0) resolves its best 'aim' target with FUN_0041f550 and stores it into actor+0x308/0x30c only if higher priority than what's already queued, then optionally boosts the unit's exposure counters (unit+0xa6/0xa8) through a random check gated by actor_scale_value_by_ally_exposure.
results.summary: Recomputes a fallback aim/backup target for the given unit and occasionally nudges its exposure tracking counters.

results.name: actor_request_backup_for_unit
results.evidence: When a unit is not exposed and its object recently took damage (obj flags bit 0x20, obj+0x39c stale time check), rolls a probability via actor_scale_value_by_ally_exposure/random_real and, if it passes and no higher-priority backup request is already queued (actor+0x308<3), records the requesting unit or its resolved shooter (via FUN_0043ea80) into actor+0x308/0x30c.
results.summary: Randomly decides whether to raise a backup-request for a unit that recently took damage, recording the responsible target for allies to respond to.

results.name: actor_notify_grenade_or_threat_direction
results.evidence: If the actor has a valid squad/cluster leader link (actor+0x18), remaps param_2 (0/1/2) to a squad-event value and calls FUN_0042d340 with code 0xb when param_1==2, then normalizes the incoming direction vector and, in low-awareness/pre-combat states, calls actor_queue_look_position before finally always calling actor_queue_search_position to clear/refresh the search queue.
results.summary: Notifies the squad of an incoming threat/grenade direction and updates the actor's look and search queues accordingly.

results.name: actor_notify_squad_event_and_search
results.evidence: If the actor has a cluster leader (actor+0x18 valid) it calls FUN_0042d340 with code 0x17 or 0x16 depending on in_CL; if param_1 is set and no higher-priority search is queued (actor+0x308<6) it also sets actor+0x308/0x30c to a fixed search request with no specific position (0xffffffff).
results.summary: Sends a squad notification event and optionally raises a generic search request for the actor.

results.name: actor_boost_accuracy_after_alert
results.evidence: Only runs while actor+0x358 is set and the actor definition's 'search' field (offset 0x334 via the definition pointer) is positive; clears the flag, picks a variant index via FUN_006391b4 into actor+0x35a, and if the current target is close (<4.0), raises the smoothed accuracy value (actor+0x354) toward at least 1.8 when it was already above that.
results.summary: Once an alert condition clears, resets the alert flag, records a random variant, and nudges the actor's smoothed accuracy upward if its target is nearby.

results.name: actor_evaluate_charge_trigger
results.evidence: Uses actor_get_actor_definition and FUN_00569c90 to gate on the actor being in a valid charge-eligible state (awareness>=5, not close-range already), compares target distance (target+0x11c) against definition thresholds (def+0x74/def+0x16c), checks a per-object 'aggressive' flag (obj+0x106<0), and, once triggered, runs a probabilistic roll (weighted by nearby friendly/enemy counts, actor+0x200/0x245 style tallies) stored into actor+0x362; this is invoked as case 5 of actor_update_charge_decision's charge-trigger switch.
results.summary: Evaluates the 'custom' charge-trigger condition for melee/charge behavior, combining distance thresholds, aggression flags, and a randomized roll weighted by nearby allies and enemies.

results.name: actor_pick_dialogue_variant_a
results.evidence: Advances the actor's RNG stream (DAT_00719cd0) when in_AX is 1, 2, or 3, then returns a clamped (<=0xff) result of FUN_006391b4, matching the 'pick sound/line variant index' helper used to fill the actor+0x546 dialogue-variant field elsewhere.
results.summary: Advances the actor's RNG for certain dialogue categories and returns a clamped random dialogue-variant index.

results.name: actor_pick_dialogue_variant_b
results.evidence: Near-identical to actor_pick_dialogue_variant_a but advances the RNG for in_AX==1 or 1<in_AX<4 instead of 1/2/3 individually, otherwise returning the same clamped FUN_006391b4 result.
results.summary: Variant of actor_pick_dialogue_variant_a with a slightly different RNG-advance condition, used for a different dialogue category.

results.name: swarm_component_compute_avoidance_offset
results.evidence: Walks the swarm entry referenced by actor+0x28 (DAT_0088035c array, stride 0x98) looking for the swarm-component slot matching param_2, then, depending on component flags (swarm_component+0x21 bits 4/0x10), either derives an offset from the object's velocity fields (obj+0x74/0x78 or fallback 0x80/0x84) via vector2d_normalize_with_length, or calls FUN_004beb30 to compute a steering offset scaled by param_3 and clamped to that radius, writing the result into param_4.
results.summary: Computes a per-swarm-member avoidance/spacing offset vector, either mirroring the member's own velocity or invoking a steering helper, clamped to a maximum radius.

results.name: actor_dispatch_type_vtable_0x10
results.evidence: Looks up the actor-type function-pointer table (&PTR_PTR_006853b8)[actor+4] and, if the entry at offset 0x10 is non-null, calls it with no further argument marshaling visible in the decompilation.
results.summary: Invokes the per-actor-type virtual callback at vtable slot 0x10, if one is registered for this actor's type.

results.name: actor_dispatch_type_vtable_0x18
results.evidence: Unconditionally calls the per-actor-type function pointer at (&PTR_PTR_006853b8)[actor+4][0x18], the same table used by actor_dispatch_type_vtable_0x10/0x1c.
results.summary: Invokes the per-actor-type virtual callback at vtable slot 0x18.

results.name: actor_dispatch_type_vtable_0x1c
results.evidence: Same pattern as actor_dispatch_type_vtable_0x10 but checks and calls the function pointer at table offset 0x1c for the actor's type.
results.summary: Invokes the per-actor-type virtual callback at vtable slot 0x1c, if one is registered.

results.name: actors_initialize
results.evidence: Existing non-FUN_ name confirmed by the code: allocates the three module-level data arrays via FUN_005380d0 using literal strings 'actor', 'swarm', and 'swarm component', storing their handles into DAT_00880360/DAT_0088035c/DAT_00880358 respectively, matching every other function's use of those globals.
results.summary: Creates the actor, swarm, and swarm-component data arrays used by the rest of the AI actor module.

results.name: actor_new
results.evidence: Allocates a new element from the actor data array via datum_new, then bulk-initializes roughly 100 fields of the new actor record from the referenced unit definition's data (puVar2, reached through the object-table double lookup pattern), including cluster (0x58), type (0x18/4), and numerous default -1/0xffff sentinel fields.
results.summary: Allocates and default-initializes a new actor record for the unit type referenced by the given object/placement index.

results.name: actor_new_and_attach_to_unit
results.evidence: For a freshly spawned unit it validates the current object via object_try_and_get, allocates an actor with actor_new, links it to the new unit (FUN_00436770/FUN_00436940), and sets its mode (actor+0x6a) based on param_8, activating it via FUN_00427860 when non-dormant; for the squad-reuse path it instead searches existing cluster actors for a free slot matching param_3/param_5, ultimately calling FUN_00427560 or FUN_004279f0 to bind the chosen actor to the unit, and tears down via FUN_00427e60 on failure.
results.summary: Creates a brand-new actor (or reuses a compatible existing squad member) and binds it to a newly placed unit, or deletes it again on failure.

results.name: actor_initialize_unit_ai_properties
results.evidence: Copies AI-relevant fields from the unit definition (puVar2) into the live unit object (grenade timers at +0x188/+0x1b8, notice range +0x176), then conditionally spawns and attaches a primary weapon/grenade child object via object_new_with_datum_role_control and links it with FUN_0056d400/FUN_0056d1a0, finally propagating shield/flashlight-related object flags (obj+0x204, +0x37c/+0x380) from the definition's bit flags.
results.summary: Applies a unit definition's AI-related properties (grenade timing, notice range, attached weapon/child objects, shield flags) to a newly placed unit object.

results.name: actor_place_new_unit
results.evidence: Runs objects_garbage_collection, resolves the placement/unit-definition pointers through the object table, computes facing from a yaw angle (fcos/fsin), creates the object via object_new_with_datum_role_control, then calls actor_initialize_unit_ai_properties and actor_new_and_attach_to_unit to bind AI, tearing down the object with FUN_004f59d0/FUN_004f5aa0 fallback logic on placement failure.
results.summary: Creates and places a new AI-controlled unit object at a starting-location/encounter placement, applying its AI properties and binding an actor to it.

results.name: actor_spawn_additional_units
results.evidence: Loops in_DX times, each iteration re-rolling the actor's RNG stream, deriving a spawn angle via FUN_004f53a0/fcos/fsin, fetching a base position with object_get_position, creating a follower object via FUN_004f5460, activating shields (FUN_0055a500) when needed, attaching it with actor_new_and_attach_to_unit, and applying optional health/scale randomization through random_real_range and FUN_00559fa0 when param_2>0.0.
results.summary: Spawns one or more additional units around an existing actor's position and attaches new actors to them, optionally randomizing their health/scale.

results.name: actor_attach_to_unit
results.evidence: Central binding function: only proceeds if unit+500 isn't already this actor, first detaches any prior cluster/backup links (FUN_00427c90/FUN_00427e60/FUN_00427bc0), then sets actor+0x18=unit index and unit+500=actor index, copies a squad/pack id (unit+0xb8) via FUN_00436710, updates squad-member counters when a threshold (unit+0xbe>99) is met, calls FUN_004297a0, and finally toggles cluster-object bits before notifying via FUN_00569bf0.
results.summary: Binds an actor to a unit object as its controller, cleaning up any prior bindings and updating related squad/cluster bookkeeping.

results.name: actor_broadcast_value_to_controlled_units
results.evidence: Writes a caller-supplied value (unaff_SI) into obj+0xb8 for either the actor's single controlled unit (actor+0x18) when it has no cluster (actor+6==0), or for every actor sharing its cluster chain (actor+0x24 walked via obj+0x1fc), or for every swarm-component member when it belongs to a swarm (actor+0x28 into the swarm array), covering all three grouping mechanisms used elsewhere in the file.
results.summary: Propagates a caller-provided value into the object-header field of every unit the actor (or its cluster/swarm) currently controls.

results.name: actor_set_active_flag
results.evidence: Compares against the actor's stored active flag at actor+8; deactivating (in_AL==0) tears down search state (FUN_00427e00/FUN_004280b0) and any active link (FUN_00427860), copying a timestamp from DAT_006f1d6c; activating (in_AL!=0) creates a swarm if needed (FUN_00427f40) when the actor already has a cluster (actor+6!=0), and calls actor_set_units_active when transitioning from idle (actor+0x6a==0).
results.summary: Toggles the actor's active/dormant flag, tearing down or (re)establishing its cluster/swarm and activation state as appropriate.

results.name: actor_set_units_active
results.evidence: Guarded by actor+8 (has-unit) and a change in the requested active flag (actor+0x13 vs unaff_BL); for a single unit it calls FUN_004f50f0/FUN_004f5130 to (de)activate, for a cluster it walks the obj+0x1fc chain, and for a swarm it walks every swarm-component slot, in every case clearing an object-header 'already processed' bit (obj+2 bit 0) when deactivating.
results.summary: Applies an activate/deactivate transition to every unit object the actor controls, whether it is a lone unit, a cluster, or a swarm.

results.name: swarm_add_component
results.evidence: Appends a new entry (actor id in_EAX, extra data in_ECX) into the swarm's component-index arrays at swarm+0x18/+0x58 (indexed by the running count at swarm+2), initializes a matching swarm-component-array slot (DAT_00880358) to -1, increments the count, and calls FUN_00428130 (a re-sort/renumber step).
results.summary: Adds a new actor as a member of a swarm's component list and triggers the swarm's member-renumbering step.

results.name: actor_link_to_unit_cluster
results.evidence: Inserts actor (param_1) at the head of unit (param_2)'s cluster linked list (unit+0x1f8 head, actor+0x1fc/+0x200 next/prev links), allocating a swarm datum first via datum_new when the actor already has a swarm (actor+0x28), then calls swarm_add_component, and updates squad-linked-object counters (unit+0xb8) similarly to actor_attach_to_unit.
results.summary: Adds an actor to a unit's multi-actor cluster (linked list of controlling actors), creating a backing swarm entry and updating squad bookkeeping.

results.name: actor_unlink_unit
results.evidence: Given the actor's single bound unit (actor+0x18), sets an object-header 'was controlled' bit (obj+2 bit 0x40), clears an object-table bit when the unit has no melee/notice state left, calls FUN_00569bf0 to notify, resets the unit's back-reference (unit+500=-1), and decrements a squad-count field (unit+0xb8 based, only if actor+0x1c was set) before clearing actor+0x18.
results.summary: Detaches the actor from its single bound unit, updating the unit's back-reference and squad-count bookkeeping.

results.name: actor_remove_from_unit_cluster
results.evidence: Removes the given actor (in_ECX) from unit (param_1)'s cluster linked list (fixing up the neighboring +0x1fc/+0x200 links), and if the actor belongs to a swarm (actor+0x28) also removes its matching entry from the swarm-component array (compacting the array and calling datum_delete), mirroring the insertion done by actor_link_to_unit_cluster/swarm_add_component.
results.summary: Removes an actor from a unit's cluster (and its swarm's component list, if any), undoing actor_link_to_unit_cluster.

results.name: actor_clear_perceived_unit_list
results.evidence: Loops while the actor's perceived-unit list head (actor+0x50) is non-empty, calling FUN_00428470 (remove head) and FUN_0043ea20 followed by datum_delete on each iteration until the list is empty.
results.summary: Empties and frees every entry in the actor's perceived-unit list.

results.name: actor_delete
results.evidence: Full actor teardown: releases movement/pathing state via FUN_00436620 or FUN_00436990 (based on actor+9), detaches from its unit or walks and removes every cluster member (actor_unlink_unit/actor_remove_from_unit_cluster), clears the perceived-unit list (actor_clear_perceived_unit_list), scans all live data-array entries via data_iterator_next to null out any dangling reference to this actor index (+0x1c==self), then calls FUN_00430c70 and datum_delete to free the actor slot itself.
results.summary: Fully tears down and frees an actor: detaches it from its unit(s), clears its perception state, scrubs dangling references elsewhere, and deletes its datum.

results.name: actor_create_swarm
results.evidence: Only runs when the actor has no swarm yet (actor+0x28==-1): allocates a new swarm datum, initializes it with this actor's id, then walks the unit-cluster linked list (unit+0x1fc) allocating a swarm-component entry for every other actor sharing that unit's cluster and recording each one's last-known object position via object_get_position.
results.summary: Creates a new swarm record for an actor and populates it with a swarm-component entry for every actor sharing the same unit cluster.
